Q: How can I copy files from a host to a Docker container? A:

My favorite method:

Containers:

CONTAINER_ID=$(docker ps | grep <string> | awk '{ print $1 }' | xargs docker inspect -f '{{.Id}}')

File file.txt

mv -f file.txt /var/lib/docker/devicemapper/mnt/$CONTAINER_ID/rootfs/root/file.txt

or

mv -f file.txt /var/lib/docker/aufs/mnt/$CONTAINER_ID/rootfs/root/file.txt

Q: Deserialize the same JSON field into two different struct fields A:

  1. Yes, use #[serde(from = "InputCharacter")] on your "input JSON" character struct instead of your use of #[serde on fields, to create your new character structure.
    Implement your conversion logic.

  2. Use serde_json::from_str() see usage: https://docs.rs/serde_json/latest/serde_json/fn.from_str.html

As in the similar issue you probably saw: Deserialize the same JSON field into two different struct fields without implementing Deserialize manually

Q: SQL Server stored procedure passed a Biztalk XML message not returning field values when parsing the XML text A:

It looks like they are using a payload from the old SQL adapter and now using it against a stored procedure that doesn't match that stored procedure

If you create a stored procedure with standard parameters, and they regenerate the scheme from that in Visual studio to use WCF-SQL, then you don't need to shred XML, as the BizTalk adapter will take care of all of that. They just need to map to the new schema that they generated.

See Configure a port using the WCF-SQL adapter

Q: Blender VSE Audio out-of-sync when animation (video) is rendered A:

A little late to the party, but Blender still seems to have sync issues with long videos. After some debugging the audio seems to be off at a factor of 1.0555..., so it can be adjusted with ffmpeg:

ffmpeg -I 'video-from-blender.mp4' -filter_complex "[0:a]atempo=1.05555[aud]" -map 0:v -map "[aud]" -c:v copy -c:a aac -shortest 'video-fixed.mp4' -y

Q: user input variable declared in function not working in other functions/main in python? A:

This is a common mistake in python. You should declare the variable first without a value and then, when defining the function, in the first line of every def you use it, call global base2.

(But this way you need to get rid of the return.)
